title: Throughput contract breach: triage and policy anchoring
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-02-09 a subset of Dedicated customer pools started missing contractual throughput windows (10-25% below committed throughput for sustained 15+ minutes). This ticket documents the investigative timeline, temporary mitigation steps taken to protect SLAs, root-cause analysis pointing to a regressied autoscaler heuristic plus an interaction with a kernel scheduling change, and concrete follow-up actions to anchor policy and prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-09 09:02 UTC: Pager alert fired for throughput SLOs from monitoring (dedicated-pool-*-throughput-drop).
2026-02-09 09:05 UTC: Incident channel created (#incident-dedicated-throughput). Engineering on-call (Marcus Chen) started triage; initial hypothesis: noisy neighbor or transient network issue.

2026-02-09 09:12 UTC: Observed correlated autoscaler downscales across multiple pools during the same 10-minute window leading to headroom deficit; synthetic traffic showed immediate throughput improvement when pools pinned to previous size.

2026-02-09 09:40 UTC: Emergency policy applied: increase min-replicas by 20% for affected dedicated pools and enable conservative scale-down override. Immediate throughput recovered to within SLA tolerance.
2026-02-09 12:00 UTC: Short-term rollback of autoscaler v2.7 heuristic via flip flag. Telemetry collection extended to capture scale decisions and scheduling latencies.

2026-02-10 to 2026-02-25: Forensics and RCA; kernel scheduling patch 1.4.3 deployed to a subset of fleet on 2026-02-07 was correlated with higher packing variance; combined with autoscaler v2.7 change that reduced headroom floor, this produced sustained under-provisioning for certain workload shapes.
2026-03-01: Draft of mitigation and policy anchoring pushed for review; preliminary actions scheduled in this ticket.
2026-03-12: Post-incident proposal circulated; awaiting sign-off from SRE and Product for prioritized backlog items.
steps_taken: Applied immediate conservative min-replicas increase (+20%) to affected dedicated pools to restore headroom.
Flipped off autoscaler v2.7 heuristic that aggressively trimmed headroom under observed sequence-length distributions.
Deployed a temporary scheduling rollback for kernel patch 1.4.3 to a canary and compared packing variance pre/post.
Increased synthetic traffic for critical customers to validate throughput window recovery and collect post-mitigation metrics.
Opened hotfix PR to add a scale-down rate limiter and headroom reservation parameter to the autoscaler.
root_cause_summary: A two-factor interaction caused capacity shortfalls: (1) autoscaler v2.7 introduced an aggressive scale-down heuristic that reduced the minimum headroom under certain sequence-length and request burst patterns; (2) kernel scheduling change (kernel 1.4.3) increased GPU packing variance and latency tail for small-batch workloads. Individually each change was within acceptable risk, but together they reduced effective throughput below contracted guarantees for specific dedicated pools.
mitigation: Reverted aggressiveness flag in autoscaler v2.7 (temporary).
Added conservative default headroom reserve (10% of committed throughput) for Dedicated capacity customers until autoscaler policy hardened.
Introduced a scale-down per-minute cap in the autoscaler to prevent multi-step rapid downscales during transient dips.
Added a scheduling canary and packing-variance metric to the deployment pipeline for kernel upgrades.
Created an emergency runbook step: autorestore-to-previous-capacity that can be executed by SRE within 10 minutes of SLO degradation.
follow_up_actions: AUT-01: Implement permanent autoscaler policy change to incorporate model sequence-length histograms into headroom computation (owner: Priya Rao, estimate: 5).
AUT-02: Add scale-down rate limiter and min-headroom config to autoscaler flags; include default conservative values for Dedicated customers (owner: Marcus Chen, estimate: 3).
OBS-01: Instrument new metric 'packing_variance_90' and surface on Dedicated pool dashboards; create alert when variance > 2x baseline (owner: Riley Thompson, estimate: 2).
TEST-01: Add chaos test scenario in CI that simulates kernel scheduling variance + sudden request pattern shift to validate autoscaler safety (owner: Diego Morales, estimate: 5).
DOC-01: Update Dedicated incident runbook with escalation thresholds, emergency capacity commands, and communication templates (owner: Aisha Patel, estimate: 2).
POL-01: Propose SLA amendment language that clarifies acceptable maintenance windows and automated headroom strategies; review with Legal and Product (owner: Laura Kim, estimate: 3).
ROLL-01: Add automated canary gating for kernel upgrades that blocks rollouts if 'packing_variance_90' increases > 25% (owner: SRE team, estimate: 4).
communications: Incident channel: #incident-dedicated-throughput. Customer notifications: initial outbound to affected customers sent 2026-02-09 13:00 UTC with temporary mitigation note and ETA for permanent fix. Follow-ups scheduled per-customer in CRM. Internal summary emailed to Execs on 2026-02-10.
lessons_learned: Do not rely on isolated unit tests for scale decisions; need integrated CI scenarios that exercise kernel scheduling + autoscaler interplay.
Ship conservative defaults for Reserved Dedicated customers and require explicit opt-in for aggressive resource trimming.
Observability must include derived metrics (packing variance, headroom-utilization) not just raw CPU/GPU usage.
Have a fast rollback path for autoscaler policy changes (feature flag + rollback playbook).
approvals: Legal: Claire Dubois - pending review for SLA language
next_steps_status: AUT-01 and AUT-02 are highest priority for the next sprint; OBS-01 and TEST-01 are scheduled in Cycle 2026-W12. DOC-01 in progress; ROLL-01 requires SRE coordination before scheduling.
notes: This ticket should be used as the canonical incident record for Dedicated throughput contract degradations until mitigations are onboarded. Consider broadening canary criteria to include customer-specific workload shapes for high-touch customers.
